Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Detection and Characterization of Colorectal Polyps during Colonoscopy: Evidence and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention because it enables early detection and removal of premalignant lesions. However, lesions can still be missed, and endoscopic differentiation of neoplastic from nonneoplastic polyps remains variable, particularly for diminutive lesions. The potential of artificial intelligence (AI) as a supportive technology for improving both polyp detection and characterization during colonoscopy has therefore been investigated. Since early studies of convolutional neural network-based computer-aided detection (CADe), the focus has shifted from retrospective image-based validation to real-time randomized trials, meta-analyses, and clinical guideline discussions. Accumulating evidence suggests that CADe improves surrogate detection outcomes, including the adenoma detection rate (ADR), polyp detection rate, adenomas per colonoscopy, and adenoma miss rate. Although a higher ADR is associated with a lower risk of postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer, it remains unknown whether the incremental improvement in the ADR achieved by CADe translates into lower postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer incidence or colorectal cancer-related mortality. Recent multicenter data further support the effectiveness of real-time CADe systems in improving detection-related outcomes, while also indicating that benefit varies with lesion characteristics and user experience. In parallel, computer-aided diagnosis (CADx) has been developed to assist the optical characterization of colorectal polyps, particularly for diminutive lesions and potential resect-and-discard or diagnose-and-leave strategies. CADx systems using white-light imaging and structured high-confidence diagnostic rules show promise, but the clinical implementation of CADx remains less mature than that of CADe. This review summarizes current evidence for AI-assisted polyp detection and characterization and discusses limitations and future directions for integrating CADe and CADx into human-centered colonoscopy practices.

title: PmiREN3.0: a multi-omics integrated and AI-assisted encyclopedia for plant microRNA research.
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators in gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Comprehensive research on miRNAs increasingly requires the integration of large and heterogeneous datasets, together with more efficient approaches to knowledge exploration. Here, we present PmiREN3.0, a major update of the Plant MicroRNA Encyclopedia. Compared with PmiREN2.0, species/subspecies coverage increased from 179 to 340, adding 22 orders, 51 families, and 108 genera. Using the same standardized workflow and annotation criteria as previous releases, high-confidence miRNAs were identified from 5319 small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) datasets, with miRNA loci increasing from 39 751 to 87 667 and miRNA families from 7838 to 18 389. Resources and tools from previous releases were extensively updated, while six new modules were added for primary transcripts, DNA methylation, RNA modifications, stress-responsive expression, metabolic pathways, and core GRNs. PmiREN3.0 also introduces miRai+, a knowledge service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that combines a language model fine-tuned on miRNA knowledge with retrieval augmented generation. Evaluation yielded scores of 0.910 for answer relevance, 0.965 for faithfulness, and 0.906 for factual correctness. Together, PmiREN3.0 provides an expanded plant miRNA dataset and an integrated platform combining multi-omics data and AI-assisted knowledge services for plant miRNA research. PmiREN3.0 is available at https://pmiren.com/.

title: Comparison of AI-Based GRBASZero and Clinicians' Perceptual Voice Assessment with Multiparametric Voice Measures in Dysphonic Turkish-Speaking Individuals.
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between clinician-based auditory-perceptual GRBAS ratings and the outputs generated by the AI-powered GRBASZero application in individuals with dysphonia and to examine how both methods correlate with objective acoustic, aerodynamic, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). The study was conducted on 60 dysphonic individuals (following the exclusion of healthy controls to prevent distributional floor effects). Sustained /a/, /i/, /s/, /z/ phonations and reading passage samples were recorded, and aerodynamic parameters (maximum phonation time and s/z ratio), along with acoustic parameters, were analyzed using Praat software. Perceptual evaluations of the recordings were performed by 13 Speech and Language Pathologists (SLPs) using the GRBAS scale, exhibiting excellent inter-rater reliability (ICC values ranging from 0.93 to 0.97; Koo and Li, 2016), and were compared with the scores generated by the GRBASZero application. Additionally, participants completed Turkish-adapted patient-reported outcome measures, including the Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10), Voice-Related Quality of Life (VRQOL), Voice Fatigue Index (VFI), and Vocal Tract Discomfort Scale (VTDS). Significant moderate correlations were found between clinician and GRBASZero assessments for the parameters G (Grade), R (Roughness), and B (Breathiness), while weak correlations were observed for the parameters A (Asthenia) and S (Strain). Both evaluation methods demonstrated theoretically consistent relationships with objective acoustic parameters; however, unlike clinicians, the AI showed no significant correlation with aerodynamic measures. Furthermore, while clinical assessments showed significant correlations with patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), AI assessments rarely correlated with these self-perceptual scales, reinforcing the conceptual distinction between auditory-perceptual judgments and patient-perceived life impact. AI-based perceptual assessments demonstrate moderate-to-weak agreement with clinician ratings. These findings suggest that tools like GRBASZero have the potential to serve as supportive adjuncts rather than absolute objective replacements in clinical voice evaluation. Furthermore, the limited correlation between AI outputs and patient-reported outcome measures is theoretically expected, reflecting the conceptual distinction between acoustic-based perceptual judgments and patient-perceived symptom burden. Similarly, the AI's inability to correlate with aerodynamic measures highlights its limitation in capturing underlying physiological deficits beyond the acoustic signal.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Bridge to Gaps in Delirium Prediction, Detection, and Management.
abstract: Delirium affects up to one-third of hospitalized older adults and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its clinical importance and the availability of validated screening tools, current care gaps extend beyond under-recognition to inconsistent risk stratification, workforce constraints, documentation burden, fragmented intervention delivery, and practical challenges with monitoring of response. We review how artificial intelligence (AI) could bridge these gaps and distinguish model development and validation, real-world clinical implementation, and emerging concepts in delirium care. Prediction models leveraging multimodal health record data, including structured variables and unstructured clinical notes, report good discrimination for delirium risk stratification, but only a few models have been integrated into clinical practice. A live multimodal machine learning model increased targeted delirium detection, yet a pre-post comparative study found a longer length of stay; improved recognition alone therefore does not equate with improved outcomes. Natural language processing, large language models, computer vision, ambient sensing, and wearable technologies enable more continuous, objective, and less labor-intensive assessment compared with traditional screening methods, but evidence remains limited with concerns about false positives and generalizability. AI-supported delirium management through reinforcement learning and digital twins is currently largely conceptual. Responsible AI adoption requires a clearly defined intended use, external validation, action pathways, equitable performance, privacy and security, consent and transparency, clinician oversight, patient preferences, and post-deployment monitoring. AI is most defensible as an adjunct that connects evidence-based delirium care to reliable execution rather than as a replacement for clinical assessment. Prospective comparative studies should evaluate patient outcomes, resource use, and balancing measures.
venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

title: Clinical Praat Parameters and Cepstral Representations for Speaker-Independent Voice Pathology Detection: The Influence of Age and Dysphonia Severity.
abstract: To determine whether clinically validated Praat parameters discriminate pathological from healthy voice under speaker-independent evaluation of the complete Saarbrücken Voice Database corpus of sustained vowels, how their performance compares with a high-dimensional cepstral representation and a speech foundation model trained through self-supervision, and how discrimination depends on dysphonia severity and on the age difference between groups. Retrospective analysis of a publicly available voice database. The machine learning task was formulated as binary classification: healthy versus pathological voice. All 15,442 sustained vowel recordings from 1288 sessions of 1180 speakers (age 27.9 ± 11.7 years in healthy and 50.7 ± 15.4 years in pathological speakers) were analyzed. A total of 78 features were extracted: 14 clinical parameters via Praat and 64 cepstral, spectral, and energy descriptors via librosa. Group differences were tested at the session level with Mann-Whitney U, quantified by rank-biserial correlation, and corrected by Holm-Bonferroni. Six classifiers were compared using nested cross-validation with five folds grouped by speaker. The severity of acoustic alteration was estimated with the Acoustic Voice Quality Index (AVQI), which does not replace perceptual evaluation, and age was controlled by matching patients to controls on age and sex and by reweighting the training data. Nine of 11 parameters reached medium effect size, led by jitter PPQ5 (r = -0.414) and CPPS (r = +0.382). Sixty percent of pathological sessions had acoustic voice quality within the healthy range. The SVM (0.775 ± 0.019) and XGBoost (0.770 ± 0.013) reached the highest recording-level AUC; adapted wav2vec 2.0 reached 0.726 ± 0.015. The 14 Praat parameters and the 52 cepstral coefficients performed similarly (AUC difference +0.014, 95% CI -0.002 to +0.030); neither equivalence nor superiority was demonstrated. With age controlled, XGBoost reached a session-level AUC of 0.721 (95% CI 0.669 to 0.769). Discrimination increased progressively across strata of acoustic alteration defined by the AVQI: 0.60 within the healthy range and 0.89 to 0.99 above it. Jitter, shimmer, and CPPS kept their effect sizes after age matching, whereas f Acoustic analysis of sustained vowels identifies dysphonia with measurable acoustic alteration but not acoustically mild disorders, and 14 interpretable parameters performed similarly to a cepstral representation nearly four times larger. Discrimination reported on the SVD should be interpreted in the light of the age difference between groups and the severity composition of the sample.

title: Development and validation of early warning scores predicting 24 h mortality addressing intercurrent medical interventions in Denmark: a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 2·08 million hospital encounters.
abstract: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is widely used to predict patient deterioration, but retrospective validations face intervention bias and emphasise discrimination performance over clinical utility. We aimed to compare the clinical net benefit of NEWS against simplified scoring rules and machine learning models, to determine whether simpler approaches suffice or if complex models offer meaningful advantages, and to evaluate performance heterogeneity across patient subgroups. In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, we included data from 15 Danish hospitals (ten hospital networks) across the Capital and Zealand regions of Denmark, between Oct 16, 2018, and Oct 16, 2023. We included all adults (aged ≥18 years) with a hospital encounter with at least one NEWS assessment. Demographic and clinical data, NEWS data, and time of death were extracted from hospital and regional electronic health records. Patients were followed up until death or completion of the 24 h observation period after the initial NEWS score was recorded, whichever occurred first. The outcome was all-cause mortality within 24 h of the initial NEWS recording. We compared NEWS against both simpler and more complex approaches for predicting 24 h mortality: simplified NEWS (NEWS without blood pressure and temperature), Demographic Early Warning Score (DEWS; simplified NEWS with age and sex), and a model based on Extreme Gradient Boosting Early Warning Score (XGB-EWS) incorporating vital signs, demographics, laboratory markers, plus medical history embeddings extracted using sentence transformers. We used propensity score weighting to mitigate intervention bias and evaluated performance using net benefit, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and calibration. This study included data for 2 080 765 hospital encounters representing 825 200 unique patients over 5 years. The majority (50·9%) of the weighted population was aged 18-65 years, 50·4% were female, 49·6% were male, and 66·2% were admitted to internal and acute medicine clinical specialties. Decision curve analysis in the overall population showed maximum net benefit differences of 1·9 additional correct mortality identifications per 10 000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS, and 1·5 per 10 000 patients between NEWS and simplified NEWS. However, stratified analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: in the high-risk group (initial NEWS ≥7), XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 78·1 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, whereas simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum performance loss of 60·2 per 10 000 patients. Conversely, in the low-risk group (NEWS 0-4), differences were minimal: XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 0·9 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, while simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum loss of 0·1 per 10 000 patients. Model complexity produced small average clinical utility gains, concentrated among patients initially classified as high risk by NEWS. These findings support prospective trials of risk-stratified monitoring based on the first NEWS assessment, testing simplified approaches for lower-risk patients while retaining full NEWS or electronic health record models for higher-risk patients. Novo Nordisk Foundation.

Deep Learning-Based Gadolinium-Free Virtual Contrast-Enhanced MRI for Predicting Immediate HIFU Ablation Outcomes in Uterine Fibroids.
abstract: Accurate assessment of microvascular perfusion is essential for predicting high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids. Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) is widely used for vascular evaluation; however, gadolinium-based agents pose safety concerns and may interfere with temperature monitoring. This study aimed to generate synthetic CE-T1WI (Syn-CE-T1WI) from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) using deep learning for predicting immediate HIFU ablation outcomes. A mask-guided 3D conditional generative adversarial network (3D-cGAN) was developed using magnetic resonance imaging data from 300 patients (240 training, 60 testing). Syn-CE-T1WI was generated from T2WI. Image quality was assessed using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and mean absolute error (MAE). Three radiologists performed blinded evaluations of image authenticity and quality. A binary classification task was used to compare Syn-CE-T1WI and Real-CE-T1WI for predicting HIFU outcomes. In the test set, PSNR was 27.05 ± 2.21 dB, SSIM was 0.825 ± 0.12, and MAE was 0.023. Radiologists achieved a mean accuracy of 52.8% in distinguishing real from synthetic images (all P > 0.05). Overall, 88.9% of Syn-CE-T1WI were rated clinically acceptable. For outcome prediction, Syn-CE-T1WI achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.713-0.763, comparable to Real-CE-T1WI (0.725-0.775; all P > 0.05). Combining Syn-CE-T1WI with T2WI yielded AUCs of 0.775-0.800, numerically higher than T2WI alone (0.713-0.763), and similar to T2WI + Real-CE-T1WI (0.800-0.813; all P > 0.05). The mask-guided 3D-cGAN enabled the generation of high-fidelity, gadolinium-free Syn-CE-T1WI that may support noninvasive prediction of immediate HIFU ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids.
